title: The soul of Jesus experienced both states
english: From the interpretation of Psalm 15: But indeed, the soul of Jesus had experience of both states. For it came to be in the region of human souls, and having come to be outside the flesh, it lives and subsists.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is explaining that the soul of Jesus has experience of both the realm of human souls and existence apart from the flesh.

title: The soul and flesh of Jesus are of the same substance as human souls and flesh
english: Therefore the soul of Jesus is rational and of the same substance as the souls of human beings, just as his flesh is of the same substance as human flesh, having come forth from Mary.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is concluding his argument that the soul of Jesus is rational and of the same substance as human souls, just as his flesh is of the same substance as human flesh, having come from Mary.

title: One person, not one nature
english: From Eustathius of Antioch, from his interpretation of Psalm 15: “God sent his Son, born of a woman” (Galatians 4:4). I did not say “born ones,” but “born,” for the person is singular. I did not say the nature is singular—away with it, may it not be! Nor did I say that flesh and divinity have the same substance. Rather, I said one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, known in all things in the difference of the natures.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is closing his interpretation of Psalm 15 by quoting Galatians 4:4 and explaining that the singular 'born' points to Christ's one person, not one nature.
